text: Someone wronged you. And now... you have the upper hand. What do you do?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Two men stood in that exact moment... centuries apart.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: One was a duke in Renaissance Italy. He chose to hope... and it ruined him.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: The other was a warrior in one of Rumi's stories. He chose the opposite... and won something no battle could give him.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Tonight, Machiavelli and Rumi answer one of the oldest questions there is. What do you do... with an enemy?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Florence... fifteen thirteen.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Niccolo Machiavelli has lost his government job. He has been jailed... and tortured. Now he lives on a small farm outside the city... writing a short book about power.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: He calls it The Prince. And one of its main characters... is a man he had watched up close. Cesare Borgia.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Borgia's father was Pope Alexander the Sixth. With his father's power behind him... Borgia built a state of his own.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Then, in the summer of fifteen oh three... his father died. And Borgia himself was so sick... he was close to death.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Machiavelli says Borgia told him he had planned for everything his father's death could bring... everything, except being close to death himself.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Now Rome had to choose a new Pope. Borgia could not pick the winner... but he could still block one.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: And he let a man through. A cardinal he had injured in the past... a man with every reason to fear him. That man became Pope Julius the Second.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Why would Borgia allow it? Because he hoped. He hoped fresh favours would wash away old wounds.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Machiavelli's answer is ice cold. He who believes that new benefits will cause great personages to forget old injuries... is deceived.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: And his verdict on Borgia? The duke erred in his choice... and it was the cause of his ultimate ruin.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Look at what the mistake really was. Not cruelty. Not weakness. Wishful thinking.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Machiavelli explains it in seven words. For men injure either from fear or hatred.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Someone you once hurt... may still be afraid of you. And fear, handed power, tends to strike first.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Picture an office. Last year, Maya took credit for a teammate's idea... in front of everyone.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: This year, she's friendly. Coffee. Compliments. A birthday card.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Then a promotion opens up... and that teammate sits on the hiring panel.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Does a birthday card erase that meeting? Machiavelli would say... don't bet your future on it.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: His lesson isn't revenge. It's clear sight. Know who you have hurt. Repair it honestly... or prepare for it. But never just hope.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Machiavelli has a second idea about enemies. And this one... is strangely hopeful.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: In chapter twenty, he writes that leaders become great by overcoming what stands against them. Fortune even sends a new leader enemies... so that he can rise.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: By them to mount higher... as by a ladder which his enemies have raised.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Read that again. Every person who doubted you... every door that was shut in your face... can become a rung.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: A girl is cut from her school's basketball team. The coach says she's too slow.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: That sentence becomes her alarm clock. Five in the morning. Every day. For a year.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Next season, she makes the team. The coach never trained her... but he built the ladder.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: And Machiavelli goes one step further. He noticed that new rulers often found more loyalty in people they first distrusted... than in the ones they trusted from the start.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Why? Because a former rival who joins you has something to prove. They have to show, by what they do... that you were wrong about them.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: So today's opponent could be tomorrow's most loyal partner... if you leave the door open.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Now... travel east. To Rumi.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: In the thirteenth century, he wrote the Masnavi... a vast poem, full of stories.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: One of them is about Ali, the great warrior of early Islam... whom the story calls the Lion of God.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Ali is locked in a fight with an enemy chief. And Ali is winning. The fight is almost over.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Then the beaten man does the one thing he has left. He spits in Ali's face.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Stop the story right there. Every instinct says... strike. Anyone watching would understand.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Instead, Rumi's story goes like this. Ali, instead of taking vengeance on him, at once dropped his sword... to the Magian's great astonishment.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: The enemy can't believe it. Why spare me? Why now... right after I insulted you?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: In essence, Ali's answer is this. He fought for a cause... not for his own pride.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: The moment that spit made it personal, anger had entered the fight. And a fight run by anger... was not one he was willing to win.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: The story says that one act won what the sword never could. The enemy chief... and his whole family... came over to Ali's faith.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Now look at that spit again. It was a weapon... the last one the enemy had.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: He couldn't win the fight anymore. So he tried to win Ali's temper.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: If Ali had struck in rage, the enemy would still have been in control of him... for one final second.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: That's Rumi's point. The enemy in front of you is beaten in a moment. The anger inside you... keeps fighting long after.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: So who is right? The cold strategist... or the poet?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: At first, they sound like opposites. Machiavelli says, never forget an old injury. Rumi says, drop the sword.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: But look closer. Borgia lost because he let hope make his decision. Ali won because he refused to let anger make his.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Same lesson... from two sides. When an enemy is near, don't let a feeling take the wheel.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Machiavelli is the mind. See your enemy exactly as they are. Not better. Not worse.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Rumi is the heart. See yourself exactly as you are... and notice the moment a fight becomes about your pride.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: A message from a rival lands at midnight. Sharp. Built to sting.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: The mind asks... what can this person really do to me? The heart asks... what does my anger want me to do? And whose plan is that?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Most of the time... the angry reply is exactly the move they were hoping you'd make.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: So here's one thing to try... today.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Think of one person you'd call a rival. At work, at school, online.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Take a piece of paper. On the left, write what they could really do to you. Be honest, not hopeful. That's Machiavelli.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: On the right, write what your anger wants to do to them. That's Rumi's battlefield. Then... don't do it.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Instead, pick one move that makes you stronger. One rung... on the ladder they built for you.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Now tell me. Which is harder for you? Seeing an enemy clearly... or putting down the sword? Mind, or heart? Write it in the comments.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Follow Awaaz Mindset... where Machiavelli and Rumi meet every week.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: He had his enemy beaten... and he dropped his sword. Why?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Next time someone pokes at you... wait one breath, and ask. Is this my move... or theirs?
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

text: Could you have dropped the sword? Tell me below.
name: en-US-ChristopherNeural

name: en-US-ChristopherNeural
